stories.kick: Weather · Energy · Press ✓ 9 outlets · damage not yet confirmed
stories.hl: Isaias comes ashore in the Florida Panhandle as a Category 2 hurricane. Nearly three-quarters of Gulf oil output is shut in
stories.dek: The first Atlantic hurricane of the season weakened from a major Category 3 before landfall near Destin on Friday night, but forecasters still warned of life-threatening storm surge. Damage reports were not confirmed, and oil traders get their first look when futures reopen.
body: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, at about 8:30 p.m. local time on Friday as a Category 2 storm with 105 mph winds, NBC News reported, and Politico described a dangerous hurricane coming ashore along the Gulf Coast. Earlier in the day Isaias had been a major Category 3 with winds up to 120 mph, according to PBS NewsHour and CBS News, before it weakened on its approach. NPR called it the season’s first Atlantic hurricane. The National Hurricane Center, as relayed by DW and NBC, still warned of life-threatening storm surge, extreme winds and possible tornadoes, and CBS had put the surge at up to 9 feet. Florida and Alabama declared states of emergency, NBC reported, and ABC said several Panhandle counties ordered evacuations. By late evening NBC’s correspondents described conditions deteriorating fast in Pensacola and across the Panhandle as the eye moved onshore. We have not seen a confirmed count of damage, injuries or deaths, so we are not reporting one. The Financial Times said the storm was headed toward Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi, so the danger now moves inland with rain, wind and power outages.

The storm also hit the oil patch. Bloomberg reported that nearly three-quarters of oil production in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico was shut in, and CBS said Chevron and Shell were halting output and evacuating offshore platforms. CNBC and MarketWatch noted that the hurricane arrives when fuel markets are already tight because of the wars in Eastern Europe and the Middle East. Bloomberg said Gulf Coast crude prices rose. West Texas Intermediate settled at $91.85 on Friday, and diesel is the sensitive spot: prices are near a record, the Japan Times reported, 24 days before the midterm elections. Delta Air Lines separately cut its 2026 profit forecast because a $6 billion jump in fuel costs outweighed higher fares, Reuters reported, a sign of how fuel prices already reach travelers and shippers. Producers usually restart within days if platforms are undamaged, but we found no official restart timetable. PBS explained why forecasts swung this week: a strong El Niño, whose upper winds tear storms apart, was fighting the Gulf’s unusually warm water over the hurricane’s strength. AFP Fact Check separately reported that a meteorologist retracted an AI-generated hurricane map that had spread online. Treat unsourced tracks and screenshots with caution and follow the Hurricane Center and your county emergency office. Saturday’s questions are practical. Where does the center track after landfall, how much rain falls inland, how many homes lose power, and how quickly do offshore platforms come back? State and local damage assessments will answer the last two. Quotes and figures here are as reported by the outlets named; the Hurricane Center’s own advisories were not re-read.

stories.kick: Energy · Ukraine war · Press ✓ 9 outlets · amounts as stated by Trump
stories.hl: Trump says Russia will ship diesel to the U.S. after a Putin call. Zelensky calls it an “investment in war”
body: President Trump said Friday that Vladimir Putin agreed in a phone call to release 300,000 tons of diesel immediately and millions more over coming months, CBS, Reuters, NBC, NPR, The Washington Post and The New York Times reported. The aim is lower pump prices before the Nov. 3 elections. The Times noted that Russia has an export ban on diesel, and the Post said the volume is small next to U.S. demand but lines Washington up against Ukraine’s strikes on Russian refineries. Zelensky called the plan an “investment in war,” Reuters reported. Livemint said the U.S. is temporarily easing sanctions; we saw no Treasury notice. Reuters added that earlier diesel moves have not yet lowered prices.

popup.kick: Energy · Ukraine war · Press ✓ 9 outlets · amounts as stated by Trump
popup.title: Trump says Russia will ship diesel to the U.S. after a Putin call. Zelensky calls it an “investment in war”
popup.what: President Trump said Friday that he spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin and that Russia will release 300,000 tons of diesel immediately and millions more in the coming months, according to CBS, Reuters, NBC, NPR and The Washington Post. The New York Times noted that Russia has an ongoing ban on diesel exports. The Post said the volume is small compared with U.S. demand but puts the U.S. alongside Russia and against Ukraine’s attacks on Russian refineries. Reuters reported that Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelensky, called letting Russia sell diesel to the U.S. an “investment in war,” and Politico reported he called the deal a “smokescreen.” The Kremlin said Putin downplayed an early resumption of Ukraine talks in the call, Reuters reported, while US, Ukrainian and European negotiators met in Miami. Livemint reported that the U.S. is temporarily easing sanctions; we did not see a Treasury notice.
popup.why: The deal reverses years of U.S. pressure on Moscow, and it is aimed at diesel prices that the Japan Times says are near a record. It also strains ties with Ukraine and NATO allies, as The Guardian reported.
popup.me: Diesel moves freight, farm work and many delivery costs, so it feeds into grocery and shipping prices. Reuters said earlier steps to raise supply have not yet lowered prices, and 300,000 tons is a small share of U.S. use, so do not expect relief at the pump soon.
popup.a: Prices are hurting voters and businesses, and any added supply helps. The administration says the deal is about American costs.
popup.b: Buying from Russia funds its war and rewards Putin without a ceasefire. Ukraine’s leader and Democrats such as Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz called it a mistake or a sign of desperation.
popup.say: Watch for the paperwork: a Treasury license or notice, the first cargoes, and whether Russia lifts its export ban in practice. Until a shipment arrives, this is a presidential announcement.
popup.src: CBS News · Reuters · NBC News · NPR · Washington Post · New York Times · Politico · Guardian · Japan Times · Livemint (sanctions) · Oct. 9–10

stories.hl: Stocks rise on Friday as the 10-year yield edges up
stories.dek: The S&P 500 gained 0.59% and the Dow 0.83%; the 10-year ended at 5.244%.

popup.kick: Markets · Press ✓ 4 outlets · closes from DailyDrop’s market feed
popup.title: Stocks rise on Friday as the 10-year yield edges up to 5.244%
popup.what: U.S. stocks rose on Friday: the S&P 500 gained 0.59% to 7,811.54, the Nasdaq rose 0.64% to 27,366.17 and the Dow added 0.83%, or 423.31 points, to 51,654.95, by DailyDrop’s market feed and the Straits Times. Wall Street posted weekly gains with earnings and inflation data ahead, the Straits Times reported. WTI crude rose 0.39% to $91.85 a barrel and gold gained 1.43% to $4,216.30. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 1.3 basis points to 5.244%. Bloomberg said the AI-driven strength in major indexes masks a widening retreat across markets as high oil prices and borrowing costs bite, and the Japan Times said Treasury yields are at their highest in nearly 25 years. Reuters reported that consumer sentiment deteriorated further in October, and Delta cut its profit forecast on fuel costs.
popup.why: The 10-year yield sets borrowing costs for mortgages and companies, and oil feeds inflation. Stocks are rising even as yields sit at multi-decade highs, which Bloomberg says leaves the rally dependent on AI-linked shares.
popup.me: High yields keep mortgage rates and credit card costs elevated. Retirement accounts weighted toward technology carry the most exposure if the AI rally stalls.
popup.a: Earnings and AI spending are strong enough to support valuations.
popup.b: Rising oil and yields are already hurting parts of the market, and a narrow rally is fragile.
popup.say: Markets are closed Saturday and Sunday. Monday, Oct. 12, is Columbus Day: stocks trade but bonds do not. The next hard test is September CPI on Oct. 14, then the Fed meeting on Oct. 28.
popup.src: Straits Times (Friday close; weekly gains) · Bloomberg (rate shock) · Japan Times (yields) · Reuters (consumer sentiment; Delta) · Closing levels supplied by DailyDrop’s market feed (Oct. 9)

stories.hl: NYPD releases video of the Bronx ICE shooting
stories.dek: A man was shot in the neck with a child in the back seat. DHS and the mayor disagree on what happened.

popup.kick: Immigration · Press ✓ 8 outlets · DHS and mayor’s accounts differ
popup.title: NYPD releases video of the Bronx ICE shooting. DHS and the mayor disagree on what happened
popup.what: CBS News reported that an ICE agent shot Oscar Belgal, 28, once in the neck in the Marble Hill neighborhood on Thursday, and that his child was in the back seat and was not struck. The NYPD released surveillance and body camera footage on Friday, CBS reported. The Washington Post said federal authorities allege Belgal used his car to ram government vehicles and endanger officers, and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said agents did not know the 5-year-old was in the car. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the city wants ICE out, CBS reported, and Politico said the administration rejected his demand for an enforcement freeze. The Guardian reported residents were furious and frightened. The video and the officer’s account have not been reconciled in the coverage we saw.
popup.why: The shooting is the latest in a series involving immigration agents, and it sits at the center of a fight between New York’s mayor and the federal government over enforcement in the city.
popup.me: For New Yorkers, the question is how federal operations are carried out near homes and streets. The city has limited power over federal agents, so any inquiry depends on federal agencies and courts.
popup.a: Officers face dangerous encounters, and the federal account says the man tried to ram agents with his car. Video and an investigation should decide.
popup.b: Firing into a car with a child inside cannot be squared with safe enforcement, and an independent inquiry is needed.
popup.say: Three things decide this: what the video shows about the car’s movement, what the officer says triggered the shots, and whether any independent investigation opens. The federal description comes from federal officials.
popup.src: CBS News · Guardian US · Washington Post · Politico · Oct. 9 · Federal account limited to statements by DHS officials

stories.hl: Trump sets up a committee to investigate Fed governor Cook
stories.dek: A White House hearing is set for Nov. 5 on mortgage-fraud claims she denies.

popup.kick: Federal Reserve · Press ✓ 8 outlets · allegations denied
popup.title: Trump sets up a committee to investigate Fed governor Lisa Cook, with a White House hearing Nov. 5
popup.what: President Trump created a committee to investigate allegations that Fed Governor Lisa Cook made false statements on mortgage documents, CBS, PBS, The Guardian, The Washington Post, Reuters, NBC and Politico reported. PBS said a written memo directs Cook to attend a White House hearing on Nov. 5 to answer the committee’s questions. The move follows a Supreme Court decision in June that rejected Trump’s attempt to fire her, CBS reported, and The Guardian called it a renewed effort to oust her. The Washington Post said the commission will report to the president. Cook’s response was not in the coverage we reviewed.
popup.why: The Fed’s independence from presidential pressure is at issue, and the central bank sets rates at a moment of high yields and inflation worries.
popup.me: If a president can remove a Fed governor over disputed allegations, rate decisions could become more political, which can affect mortgage and savings rates over time.
popup.a: Mortgage fraud allegations deserve review, and a committee is a lawful way to gather facts.
popup.b: The Supreme Court has already blocked the firing, and a presidential panel is a pretext to remove a governor.
popup.say: Allegations are not findings. Watch whether Cook attends on Nov. 5, whether she answers, and whether the White House tries a second dismissal that goes back to court.
popup.src: CBS News · PBS NewsHour · Guardian · Washington Post · Reuters · NBC News · Politico · Oct. 9

stories.hl: Judge rules DOJ’s state voter-roll checks unlawful
stories.dek: The policy matched voter rolls against an immigration database.

popup.title: Judge rules the Justice Department’s state voter-roll checks unlawful
popup.what: A federal judge ruled Friday that the Justice Department’s policy of collecting states’ unredacted voter rolls and checking them against a federal immigration database was unlawful, The Guardian, CBS, Reuters and The Washington Post reported. The Post identified the court as a D.C. court. CBS said the ruling strikes down the plan to press states to remove voters the department decides are registered illegally. The coverage we saw did not say whether the government will appeal.
popup.why: The ruling affects how voter lists are maintained 24 days before the midterm elections and limits what the federal government can demand from states.
popup.me: Your voter registration is not affected by this ruling directly. States keep control of their own rolls, and you can check your status with your state election office.
popup.a: Removing noncitizens from the rolls protects election integrity.
popup.b: Matching rolls against an immigration database risks wrongly purging eligible citizens, and states control their own lists.
popup.say: Watch for an appeal and a request to pause the ruling. Any emergency order would matter more than the ruling itself in the weeks before Nov. 3.
popup.src: Guardian US · CBS News · Reuters · Washington Post · Oct. 9

stories.hl: Mike Ditka, Bears coach and Hall of Famer, dies at 86
stories.dek: He led Chicago to its only Super Bowl title.

popup.title: Mike Ditka, the Chicago Bears coach and Hall of Famer, dies at 86
popup.what: Mike Ditka, the Chicago Bears player and head coach, died at age 86, according to NBC, CBS, ABC, The Guardian, The New York Times, AP, the Los Angeles Times and CNA. The Los Angeles Times said he was the first tight end inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, and CBS said he led the Bears to their only Super Bowl title. The 1985 Bears won it. The coverage we saw did not give a cause of death.
popup.why: Ditka is one of the best-known names in the NFL and the face of Chicago football for decades.
popup.me: If you follow the Bears or the NFL, expect tributes through the weekend.
popup.say: A career as a player, assistant and head coach with the same franchise is rare. Look for the team’s tribute and any funeral plans.
popup.src: NBC News · CBS News · ABC News · Guardian · New York Times · Los Angeles Times · AP · CNA · Oct. 9

stories.kick: World · Law · Press ✓ 9 outlets · reactions as reported
stories.hl: The U.S. sanctions the International Criminal Court itself, hours after Navi Pillay wins the Nobel Peace Prize
body: The Treasury Department designated the International Criminal Court for sanctions on Friday, Reuters, AP, CBS, The Washington Post, The Guardian and USA Today reported, going beyond earlier penalties on more than a dozen of its judges and other officials. The Post said the measures aim to cut the court off from the global financial system and threaten punishment for countries that do business with it. CBS reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick” unless it changes. The move came hours after the Nobel committee awarded the Peace Prize to Pillay, a former ICC judge, saying international law is “under political attack,” PBS reported.

Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom issued a joint statement backing the court, and Japan’s prime minister voiced “deep concern,” the Japan Times said. The ICC prosecutor said the work will continue, per Reuters. Trump said Norway bears an “indelible stain” for not awarding him the prize, NBC and Reuters reported. Watch how banks respond, and whether allies shield the court.

popup.kick: World · Law · Press ✓ 9 outlets · reactions as reported
popup.title: The U.S. sanctions the International Criminal Court itself, hours after Navi Pillay wins the Nobel Peace Prize
popup.what: The Treasury Department designated the International Criminal Court for sanctions on Friday, according to NHK, CBS, The Guardian, The Washington Post, Reuters, AP and USA Today. CBS said this goes beyond earlier penalties on more than a dozen of its judges and other officials. The Post said the measures aim to cut the court off from the global financial system and threaten punishment for countries that do business with it. CBS reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick” unless it changes. The sanctions came hours after the Nobel committee gave the Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, a former ICC judge and international human rights lawyer, saying international law is “under political attack,” PBS reported. A joint statement from the foreign ministries of Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands and the UK backed the court, and the ICC prosecutor said work would continue, Reuters reported.
popup.why: Sanctioning an institution, not just individuals, could hinder its banking, payroll and cooperation with other countries, and it tests whether allies will protect a court that Washington opposes.
popup.me: Little direct effect on most readers. Companies and banks that deal with the court, or with its staff, may face new compliance risk.
popup.a: The administration accuses the court of unfairly targeting Americans and allies for war crimes charges and says the U.S. does not need it.
popup.b: Allies and the Nobel committee argue that attacking a court that prosecutes war crimes weakens the international rules the U.S. helped build.
popup.say: Watch for the Treasury’s text on how long banks have to wind down dealings with the court, and whether Europe uses its blocking rules. Trump’s remark that Norway has an “indelible stain” for not picking him is a sideshow to the sanctions.
popup.src: CBS News · Guardian US · Washington Post · Reuters · AP · USA Today · PBS NewsHour · Japan Times · NHK · NBC News · Oct. 9–10

stories.kick: Military · Justice · Press ✓ 10 outlets · execution date not confirmed
stories.hl: The Pentagon plans to livestream the firing-squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter. Vance says he would not watch
body: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon will livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, the former Army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, CBS, NBC and The New York Times reported. CBS said the execution by firing squad is planned for December. Reuters noted that a government execution has never been broadcast and the military has not used a firing squad since 1945. Republicans split: Vice President JD Vance said he “is not going to be watching” and cast doubt that it would go ahead, PBS and the Times reported, while Rep. Adam Smith, a Democrat, called it “barbaric and gratuitous.”

Trump said Hasan “deserves” the firing squad, USA Today reported, but has not said whether it will be streamed, according to Reuters. PBS and the Times quoted legal experts who see a narrow path to challenge a public execution. Guardian reporting described condemnation abroad. The Pentagon has not changed its plan in the coverage we saw.

popup.kick: Military · Justice · Press ✓ 10 outlets · execution date not confirmed
popup.title: The Pentagon plans to livestream the firing-squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter. Vance says he would not watch
popup.what: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon will livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, the former Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, according to CBS, NBC and The New York Times. CBS said the execution by firing squad is planned for December. Snopes noted that a military jury sentenced Hasan to death in 2013. Reuters reported that a government execution has never been broadcast and that the military has not used a firing squad since 1945. Vice President JD Vance said he is not going to be watching and cast doubt on whether the plan will go forward, PBS and the Times reported. Rep. Adam Smith, a Democrat on the House Armed Services Committee, called the plan “barbaric and gratuitous,” CBS reported. Trump said Hasan “deserves” the firing squad, USA Today reported, but Reuters said he has not said whether it will be streamed.
popup.why: The plan raises legal, ethical and political questions at once, and it has split Republicans. It would also be the first public execution in the U.S. in roughly 90 years, as CBS and NPR described.
popup.me: Social platforms would have to decide whether to carry the footage, CBS reported. Psychiatrists told The Guardian that viewing could harm some people.
popup.a: A mass killer was lawfully sentenced, and showing the punishment is a matter of transparency and deterrence.
popup.b: Turning an execution into a broadcast is degrading, risks the families of victims and viewers, and undermines the dignity of the law.
popup.say: Watch whether Trump weighs in, whether the Pentagon changes the plan after Vance’s comments, and whether anyone besides Hasan can bring a court challenge. Experts quoted by PBS see a narrow path.
popup.src: CBS News · NBC News · New York Times · PBS NewsHour · Reuters · USA Today · Snopes · Politico · Guardian · NPR · Oct. 9–10

stories.kick: White House · Press ✓ 9 outlets · formal announcement not seen
stories.hl: Trump picks conservative commentator Katie Zacharia as his next press secretary
body: A White House official confirmed that Katie Zacharia was offered the job of press secretary, ABC, NBC, The Guardian, Politico, Reuters, USA Today, CBS and The Washington Post reported. She would replace Karoline Leavitt, who left the post at the end of August after giving birth to her second child, The Guardian said. The New York Times described Zacharia as a conservative commentator who briefly worked at the Department of Homeland Security. Outlets differ on her recent media roles, so we leave those out.
We did not see a formal announcement of a start date. The first briefing, and how she handles access for reporters, will set the tone for the final weeks before the midterms.

blocks.title: Word of the day
blocks.html:
LandfallWeather

The moment the center of a hurricane crosses the coastline. The worst weather often arrives hours before it and keeps going after it, which is why a storm’s category at landfall tells only part of the story. Isaias reached landfall on Friday night as a Category 2.

blocks.title: Unverified — what we could not confirm
blocks.html:
"The U.S. has lifted sanctions on Russian oil." One outlet says sanctions are temporarily eased. We saw no Treasury notice, and Trump described only a diesel deal.

"The Hasan execution will be livestreamed." The Pentagon says so, but Vance doubts it and Reuters reports Trump is still weighing it.

"This viral map shows Isaias’s track." AFP Fact Check reports a meteorologist retracted an AI-generated map. Use the Hurricane Center’s advisories.

blocks.title: What to watch
blocks.html:
Sat 10/10 Isaias after landfall: the inland track, rain, power outages and any confirmed damage or casualties · when Gulf platforms restart · the Hurricane Center’s advisories · reaction from Kyiv and the Treasury on the diesel deal · the Bronx shooting investigation · Zacharia’s start date.

Next week Monday 10/12 is Columbus Day / Indigenous Peoples’ Day: stocks trade, bond markets are closed · September CPI on Oct. 14 · Fed meeting Oct. 28.

For readers On the Gulf Coast, follow your county’s orders and the Hurricane Center. Elsewhere, watch diesel and gasoline: Isaias pushes them up, the Russian deal is meant to push them down.
Glossary · dotted words — economics, law, security and science terms explained in the context of the story. The list grows every day.
DailyDrop · Source ✓ = primary document checked, Press ✓ = two or more independent outlets agree · 'Take' is DailyDrop's opinion We do not reprint article text. Summaries and sources only. · © 2026

ShinyHunters.d: A cybercriminal group known for stealing data from companies and extorting them.
ShinyHunters.w: The FBI arrested a suspected member over the hack of its jobs site.

shut in.d: To stop a well or platform from producing, usually ahead of a storm.
shut in.w: Bloomberg said nearly three-quarters of Gulf oil output was shut in.

West Texas Intermediate.d: The U.S. benchmark grade of crude oil, also called WTI, priced in barrels.

Super Micro.d: A U.S. maker of servers used for artificial intelligence.
Super Micro.w: A contractor pleaded guilty to diverting its servers to China.

Navi Pillay.d: A South African jurist, former judge of the International Criminal Court and former UN human rights chief.

Cook Political Report.d: A nonpartisan newsletter that rates how competitive House, Senate and governor races are.
Cook Political Report.w: It moved 18 more House races toward Democrats.

CPI.d: The consumer price index, the main U.S. measure of inflation.

IMF-World Bank.d: The annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, where finance ministers gather.

El Niño.d: A periodic warming of the tropical Pacific that changes weather worldwide. Its upper-level winds tend to tear apart Atlantic hurricanes.
El Niño.w: PBS said El Niño's winds were fighting the Gulf's warm water over Isaias.

storm surge.d: Seawater pushed ashore by a hurricane's winds on top of the normal tide. It is usually the deadliest part of a landfall.
storm surge.w: CBS put the possible surge at up to 9 feet.

Category 3.d: A major hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale: sustained winds of 111 to 129 mph.
Category 3.w: Isaias reached Category 3, up to 120 mph, before weakening.

Starlink.w: SpaceX says it will become a major U.S. mobile carrier.

International Criminal Court.d: A permanent court in The Hague that tries individuals for war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity. The U.S. is not a member.
International Criminal Court.w: The U.S. sanctioned the court itself on Friday.

AFP Fact Check.d: The fact-checking unit of the Agence France-Presse news agency.
AFP Fact Check.w: It reported that an AI-generated Isaias map was retracted.

Bessent.d: Scott Bessent, the U.S. Treasury secretary.
Bessent.w: Reuters says he will skip the IMF meetings.

Category 2.d: A rating on the Saffir-Simpson scale, which grades hurricanes 1 to 5 by sustained wind speed. Category 2 means 96 to 110 mph winds.
Category 2.w: Isaias made landfall at Category 2 with 105 mph winds, NBC reported.

Hegseth.d: Pete Hegseth, the U.S. secretary of defense.

Fort Hood.d: A large Army base in Texas, renamed Fort Cavazos in 2023 and restored to its earlier name in 2025.

Vance.w: He said he would not watch and cast doubt on the plan.

Fed.d: The Federal Reserve, the U.S. central bank, which sets interest rates.
Fed.w: Trump is investigating one of its governors.

offshore platforms.d: Steel structures in the sea that hold equipment to drill for and produce oil and gas, evacuated before big storms.
offshore platforms.w: Operators evacuated them ahead of Isaias.

sanctions.d: Government penalties, such as asset freezes or trade limits, aimed at a country, company or person.
sanctions.w: Livemint reported temporary easing for Russia; the ICC faces new U.S. sanctions.

bond markets.d: The markets where governments and companies borrow by selling bonds. Trading in U.S. Treasuries stops on federal holidays.

hybrid.d: A vehicle that pairs a gasoline engine with an electric motor.
hybrid.w: The EU and China agreed to limit Chinese hybrid exports.

Nidal Hasan.d: The former Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009 and sentenced to death in 2013.
Nidal Hasan.w: The Pentagon plans to livestream his execution.

Karoline Leavitt.d: The White House press secretary who left the job at the end of August.

Florida Panhandle.d: The narrow strip of northwest Florida along the Gulf of Mexico, running from Pensacola east toward Tallahassee.
Florida Panhandle.w: Isaias came ashore there, near Destin.

prosecutor.d: The official who brings criminal charges. At the ICC, the prosecutor investigates and charges suspects.
prosecutor.w: The ICC prosecutor said the work will continue.

SpaceX.d: Elon Musk's rocket and satellite company, owner of Starlink.
SpaceX.w: Its mobile plans hit telecom shares.

Chevron.d: A U.S. oil major with large offshore production in the Gulf of Mexico.
Chevron.w: CBS said it was shutting production ahead of Isaias.

Destin.d: A resort city on Florida's Panhandle coast, in Okaloosa County.

Treasury.d: Short for the U.S. Treasury Department, which collects taxes, issues government debt and administers sanctions.
Treasury.w: We saw no Treasury notice easing sanctions on Russia.

Indigenous Peoples’ Day.d: A holiday on the second Monday of October that honors Native American peoples and their history. Many states and cities observe it in place of or alongside Columbus Day.

Rubio.d: Marco Rubio, the U.S. secretary of state.

landfall.d: The moment the center of a storm moves from sea over land.
landfall.w: Isaias made landfall near Destin on Florida's Panhandle.

National Hurricane Center.d: The U.S. government agency in Miami that tracks tropical storms and issues hurricane forecasts, watches and warnings.
National Hurricane Center.w: Its advisories gave the storm's wind speed and track.
